D-01_ff.reason: Three independent peer-reviewed MD studies, all matched at exact-SMILES tier in the evidence store, corroborate TraPPE-UA + lj/cut electrostatics for this exact repeat unit (*CC*): the TraPPE-UA founding parameterization paper (Martin1998), a chemistry-specific downstream validation on a C192 PE melt showing Tg=187K against an extrapolated experimental range of 185-195K in better agreement than a competing (PYS) force field (Ramos2015 -- already the resolver's own cited source), and an independent 2024 HDPE MD study using TraPPE with LJ-only nonbonded treatment at the same 14.0 A cutoff. Nothing surfaced contradicts the resolver's choice; the resolver's own evidence chain (D-01 rows citing Ramos2015 and Martin1998 verbatim) is itself corroborated rather than merely asserted.

dominant_uncertainty: Parameter-coverage risk is unmeasured, not a literature gap: no EMC trial build has confirmed TraPPE-UA can actually type this exact SMILES via the builder pipeline -- the physics choice itself is unanimously supported in the literature.

sources.claim: TraPPE PE MD study uses no explicit electrostatics method -- van der Waals/Lennard-Jones with a 14.0 A cutoff only. This matches the PHYC class's own cutoff_A=14.0 default exactly.
TraPPE-UA hydrocarbon pseudo-atoms carry no partial charges by construction (LJ 12-6 only), so PPPM/Ewald electrostatics is not needed for this force field on a purely aliphatic backbone.

Uses TraPPE (Transferable Potential for Phase Equilibria) force field for PE MD; amorphous-region density ~0.85 g/cm3 at 300 K, consistent with experimental values; LJ-only nonbonded treatment with 14.0 A cutoff, no explicit electrostatics method employed.

MD comparison of two force fields for a C192 polyethylene model (melt dynamics, glass transition, nonisothermal crystallization) found TraPPE-UA in better quantitative agreement with experimental data than the alternative (PYS) force field; simulated Tg=187.0 K vs experimental extrapolated range 185-195 K (Gordon-Taylor equation).

Founding TraPPE-UA paper: proposes united-atom Lennard-Jones 12-6 interaction parameters for n-alkane pseudo-atoms (CH2/CH3), fit to critical temperature and saturated-liquid density; nonbonded interactions are governed solely by LJ 12-6 potentials (no partial charges). Validated only against small-molecule (C1-C12) VLE/critical-point data, not bulk polymer melt -- downstream chemistry-specific validation (Ramos2015 above) is what supports PE specifically.

md_studies.title: Preparation and Characterization of High-Density Polyethylene with Alternating Lamellar Stems Using Molecular Dynamics Simulations
md_studies.note: System is high-density PE with alternating lamellar stems (semicrystalline morphology), not a simple amorphous bulk cell -- comparable for FF/electrostatics choice but not a direct density/Tg analog to this run's amorphous cell.

md_studies.title: Molecular Dynamics Simulations for the Description of Experimental Molecular Conformation, Melt Dynamics, and Phase Transitions in Polyethylene
md_studies.ensemble: melt dynamics, cooling through glass transition, nonisothermal crystallization; compared against a second (PYS) force field
md_studies.note: This is the same paper already cited by the resolver's own D-01 evidence (Ramos2015); best-comparable chemistry-specific bulk-amorphous validation of TraPPE-UA for PE, directly corroborates the class default.

md_studies.title: Transferable Potentials for Phase Equilibria. 1. United-Atom Description of n-Alkanes
md_studies.ensemble: Monte Carlo VLE/critical-point fitting (not MD, not bulk polymer)
md_studies.note: Founding parameterization paper only -- validates the LJ functional form and charge-free construction of TraPPE-UA via small-molecule VLE, not a bulk-polymer MD result; chemistry-specific PE validation rests on Ramos2015, not this paper directly.

notes: PolyDatabase (db/query_polydatabase.py) returned "not_ingested" for polyethylene -- a soft miss, not a blocker -- so no fresh WebSearch was needed since the evidence store already held three exact-SMILES, peer_reviewed_doi hits fully covering force field, electrostatics, and Tg target, all agreeing with the resolver's own citations.
